title: What Is a Direct Attach Copper (DAC) Cable
summary: This article explains Direct Attach Copper (DAC) cables, which are copper-based cabling solutions used for short-distance high-speed network connections in data centers, typically for 10Gbps to 100Gbps applications between switches and servers.
problem_solved: Provides cost-effective, low-latency connectivity solutions for short-distance data center network connections as an alternative to expensive fiber optic cables.
why_valuable: DAC cables offer significant cost savings over fiber optics for short-range connections while maintaining comparable bandwidth performance, making them ideal for data center rack-to-rack or switch-to-server connections.
